rounds.change: joints read off the photo, depth from true bone lengths, cones for limbs
rounds.lesson: limbs far too thin; a mannequin's limbs are as wide as its joints

rounds.change: lathe-profile limbs with the bulge high (Bridgman), bigger joints, chest, head
rounds.lesson: thickness was most of the miss; the pose was already right

rounds.change: wider feet and pelvis, thicker thighs
rounds.lesson: kept for the better-looking feet; silhouette unchanged

rounds.change: feet: longer paddles centred near the ankle (heel behind), wider
rounds.lesson: a mannequin foot is a paddle with a heel behind the ankle, not a point hanging past it

rounds.change: legs: thigh 28->24 top radius with less bulge, shin 19->23 (near-even pegs)
rounds.lesson: I gave it a human thigh; a wooden mannequin's legs are near-even pegs, thigh barely wider than shin. Measure the miss per limb before choosing what to change.
the leg lesson holds one limb up: a mannequin forearm is nearly as thick as its upper arm. limbs.py (per-limb miss) picks the change.
I read joints off the limb's outer edge; a joint sits on the limb's centre line. A size change that scores flat (head) means the miss is placement.
Equal-width blue and orange bands on opposite sides of a part mean it is shifted, not mis-sized: move it toward the orange. Gain +0.012; the next flat rep switches pose.

rounds.change: foot ellipsoid depth radius 14->20 (wedge, not slipper); sweeps of foot size, t and ankle placement all within 0.866-0.871
rounds.lesson: When every sweep on the top miss scores within 0.005, the pose has given what it can teach; switch to a new pose rather than polishing.

method: build.py (bpy 5.2, headless) builds 30 named parts, renders silhouette + shaded from the photo's orthographic camera and exports GLB; parts.py renders each part alone; score.py gives IoU against the private mask.
